cards.text: One afternoon, Peter and John, two of Jesus' apostles, are heading up to the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour. Nothing special, just two friends going to pray. Friend, hold onto your apron.
Meanwhile, a man who's been lame from birth is being carried to the temple gate called Beautiful. Every single day they set him down there to beg from the people going in.

cards.question: The lame man at the gate called Beautiful sees Peter and John about to go in, and he asks them for ___.

cards.text: Peter looks right at him, so does John, and Peter says, "Look at us!" I bet this man has spent all day watching feet walk past, and now somebody wants EYE CONTACT.

cards.question: When the lame man gives Peter and John his attention, he's expecting to get something from them.

cards.text: Then Peter tells him he's got no silver or gold, but what he has, he'll give. Friend, if I had my hand out and somebody opened with NO SILVER, NO GOLD, my mustache would already be waving goodbye.

cards.question: Peter has no silver or gold for the lame man. In whose name does Peter tell him to get up and walk?

cards.text: Peter reaches down, takes the man by the right hand and helps him up. Friend, lean in, because here it comes.

cards.question: Once Peter helps him up, the lame man's feet and ankles get strong slowly over the next few days.

cards.text: He SPRINGS to his feet and starts walking, a man who was lame from BIRTH. I bend over to pick up one dropped chocolate chip and I need a minute, a deep breath and a pep talk.

cards.question: The man who was lame can walk now. Where does he go with Peter and John?

answers.text: Down to the Pool of Siloam
Out to the Mount of Olives

cards.question: In the temple courts, the healed man is walking and leaping. What else is he doing?

cards.text: Now all the people see him walking and praising God. And they know that face.

cards.question: The people in the temple courts recognize the man walking and praising God. Who do they know him as?

answers.text: The man who begged at the Beautiful Gate
A servant of the high priest

cards.question: When the people see the man who used to beg, they're filled with wonder and amazement at what happened to him.

cards.text: The man clings to Peter and John. I bet you couldn't pry him off those two with a spatula.

cards.question: All the astonished people come running to Peter and John in the walkway called ___ Colonnade.

cards.text: Peter sees the whole crowd staring at him and John like they just pulled a rabbit out of a chef's hat. So he speaks up: "Men of Israel, why are you surprised by this?"

cards.question: Peter tells the crowd that he and John made the man walk by their own power and godliness.

cards.text: Peter says the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob has glorified His servant Jesus, the same Jesus they handed over and rejected before Pilate, the Roman governor. Friend, Peter is NOT warming up with small talk.

cards.question: Peter brings up Pilate. What had Pilate decided to do with Jesus?

cards.text: Peter says they rejected the Holy and Righteous One and asked for somebody else to go free instead. They had THE Holy and Righteous One, friend, and they went, "Nah, we'll take the other guy."

cards.question: Instead of the Holy and Righteous One, Peter says the people asked for a ___ to be released to them.

cards.text: Peter tells them straight out that they killed the Author of life, but God raised Him from the dead. Friend, I need three deep breaths just to admit to MYSELF that a batch came out burnt.

cards.question: Peter tells the crowd that God raising Jesus from the dead has witnesses, and that he is one of them.
Peter points to the man the crowd sees and knows. How does Peter say this man was made strong?

answers.text: By faith in the name of Jesus
By the prayers of the priests
By a gift from the temple

cards.text: Then Peter's voice gets gentle. "And now, brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, as did your leaders."

cards.question: Peter says God foretold through all the prophets that His Christ would suffer.
Peter tells the crowd to repent and turn back, so that their sins may be ___.

cards.text: Peter says turning back is so times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and so He may send Jesus, the Christ appointed for them. Friend, after all my years in a dusty drawer, TIMES OF REFRESHING might be the best three words I've ever heard.

cards.question: Peter says heaven must take Jesus in until a certain time comes. What time is that?
Peter quotes Moses, Israel's great leader, who said God would raise up a prophet like him. What did Moses say the people must do?

answers.text: Listen to Him in everything He says
Build Him a brand new temple
Wait for Him to show a sign

cards.text: And Moses didn't sugarcoat the other side either. Everyone who doesn't listen to Him will be completely cut off from among his people.

cards.question: Peter says Moses was the only prophet who ever spoke about these days.

cards.text: Peter tells them they're sons of the prophets and of the covenant God made with their fathers, when He told Abraham, "Through your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed." Not some families, friend. Not just the ones in your group chat. ALL of them.

cards.question: Peter says God raised up His Servant and sent Him to the crowd first to bless them. How does Peter say He blesses them?

answers.text: By turning each of them from their wicked ways
By giving each of them silver and gold
By making each of them rulers of nations

cards.text: We're pulling this batch out of the oven for now, friend. But I promise you, this story's still got more in the bowl.

findings.problem: The card adds that Peter and John are two of Jesus' apostles. Acts 3:1 names them and describes their trip to the temple, but it does not provide that identification, so the outside fact needs its own reference.

rule.text: Every fact and every verse number comes from that text. Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card identifies Pilate as the Roman governor. Acts 3:13 names Pilate but does not give that identification, and no reference for the outside fact is supplied.

rule.text: Every fact and every verse number comes from that text. Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The question introduces Moses as Israel's great leader. Acts 3:22 does not provide that identification, so this outside fact needs its own reference.

rule.text: Every fact and every verse number comes from that text. Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has four sentences: the main retelling followed by 'Not some families, friend.', 'Not just the ones in your group chat.', and 'ALL of them.' That exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
